patch.value: flag-invocation-parity only iterates declared flags, so 21 runtime options across 8 core commands have no flag contract

Measured 2026-09-04 on the 2026.9.4 build by walking every option Commander registers in buildCoreCommandProgram() against the flag contract the SDK resolves for the same command. Twenty-one runtime options across eight core commands have no contract row: config --value; list-all --status; next --include-decisions; update-many --status --assignee --parent --blocked-by --blocked-reason --unblock-note plus the three snake_case aliases; append --text; merge --message --force --include-reconciled; learnings --stdin --file --edit --delete; test --list. The item command has no contract resolver at all.

The parity gate cannot see any of this by construction: verifyCoreFlagInvocationParity filters observed options to declaredFlags.has(flag) before comparing arity, so it iterates its own declared list and indexes into the runtime, the inverse of the direction that would catch drift. Consequences already visible: pm contracts --command merge --flags-only omits --message and --force even though pm merge --help documents both for reconcile; pm contracts --command learnings omits the stdin, file, edit, and delete inputs the help lists; any contract-derived validator reads a skill fence instructing pm merge reconcile --message as an unknown flag.

Acceptance: the parity gate fails on any observed core option absent from the declared contract, with a negative control that seeds one undeclared option; each of the 21 options is declared or removed, with lexicon and help-token budgets re-ratcheted through governance rather than silenced; item receives a contract resolver or leaves the core program; contracts snapshot, MCP declared keys, and completion regenerate from the corrected table.
